output.name: Tormesk
output.myth: Eleven rowers took a long boat out past the last light, because Tavo laughed at them. The Ebb Hound rang his teeth at them from the west. Ahead, in the east, hung the kite Aun did not fly, and they pulled for it. The wind came round behind them and the boat would not turn for any prayer. So they rowed on in the dark. With each stroke one of them let go of a name: first the one his mother used at the hearth, then the one his wife used, then the one that meant brave. The water took them one at a time as payment for the crossing. Only the oars were left, because the sea does not want oars. Mother Hesk counted them at the Reel and wrote eleven in her book. Kael still casts for them and never catches one. If you row past your own name, do not turn to look for it. Count your strokes instead, and you will get home, though you will be known by the number.
output.finding: Start at the Ebb Hound, low in the western sky, and look one hand-span (about 19°) east of it to find Tormesk.
